options.text: Outside parking areas on autobahns and clearways for motor vehicles only
Near or on sharp bends
At bus stops

correct_answers.text: Outside parking areas on autobahns and clearways for motor vehicles only

comment: In general, the road traffic act prohibits stopping at the traffic areas when stopping is dangerous for other road users or endangers public safety and order. This is especially true for holding on the lanes of the freeway or on a highway. The same goes for sharp and confusing curves.

options.text: On narrow roadways opposite driveway entrances and exits
At taxi ranks
Immediately behind pedestrian crossings

correct_answers.text: On narrow roadways opposite driveway entrances and exits

comment: A parking ban in accordance with the road traffic act applies in all places where other road users can be obstructed or the public order and safety is no longer guaranteed by parked cars. For example, parking is prohibited at taxi stands, narrow lanes or entrances and exits in front of property as well as on and up to 5 m before pedestrian crossings.

question_text: Who has priority at this parking space?

options.text: The white vehicle, because it has arrived at the parking space first
No one, both drivers should agree
Me, because I am parking by driving in forwards

correct_answers.text: The white vehicle, because it has arrived at the parking space first

comment: The vehicle that reaches the parking space first always has priority. Priority will also be given in the event that the vehicle drives past the parking space just in order to park backwards or perform other movements that are useful for parking in this gap. Priority is also maintained when the vehicle is waiting at the parking space.

question_text: Both cars want to park here. Which car takes precedence?

options.text: The red car
The white car

comment: In this case, the red car has right of way. He has reached the parking space first. Priority will also be given in the event that the vehicle drives past the parking space just in order to park backwards or perform other movements that are useful for parking in this gap.

question_text: Up to which permissible total mass may motor vehicles be parked on specially designated footpaths?
comment: Vehicles with a maximum permissible gross vehicle weight of up to 2.8 tonnes may be parked on specially marked sidewalks.

question_text: What is the minimum distance a vehicle must leave clear in front of traffic lights if the traffic lights would be concealed by the vehicle?
comment: A minimum distance of 10 meters must be maintained so that the view of light signals is not obscured.

question_text: Where are you allowed to park a trailer with a permissible total mass exceeding 2 t in built-up areas regularly on sundays and public holidays and between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.?

options.text: In industrial areas
In wholly residential areas, on specially designated parking spaces
In special areas reserved for recreation purposes, on sufficiently wide roads

correct_answers.text: In wholly residential areas, on specially designated parking spaces

comment: Parking a trailer with a maximum authorized mass of more than 2 t is permitted in commercial and residential areas with appropriately marked parking spaces. Within closed areas and in special areas for recreational purposes, regular parking is prohibited from 22:00 to 6:00 and on Sundays as well as on public holidays.

question_text:
What must you remember when parking a trailer without a truck?
The trailer

options.text: - may not be parked for more than 2 weeks on public roads
- may be parked for more than 2 weeks on specially designated parking spaces
- may be parked for an unlimited period of time on adequate hard shoulders

correct_answers.text: - may not be parked for more than 2 weeks on public roads
- may be parked for more than 2 weeks on specially designated parking spaces

comment: Please note that you may not leave your vehicle trailers on regular parking spaces for more than two weeks if they are not attached to a towing vehicle. Incidentally, the same also applies to hard shoulders. Accordingly marked parking lots are excluded from this regulation.

question_text: You want to park on the right-hand edge of the road. What should you do in this situation?

options.text: I forego the parking space, even though I have priority
I park now, because I have priority

correct_answers.text: I forego the parking space, even though I have priority

comment: You signalled first and therefore have priority to the parking space. To avoid a conflict, you should still give up the parking space.

question_text: You want to park on the right-hand edge of the road. Who has priority in this situation?

options.text: The [blue] car has priority
I have priority
No one has priority. We have to agree

comment: The car that stopped in front of you signaled first and therefore had priority in the parking lot. If you park now, there could be a collision.

question_text: You want to reverse park on the right-hand side of the road. What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I closely observe the oncoming traffic before manoeuvring into the space
I anticipate that vehicles may exit their parking spaces
I switch on my hazard lights

correct_answers.text: I closely observe the oncoming traffic before manoeuvring into the space
I anticipate that vehicles may exit their parking spaces

comment:
When parking, you always have to pay attention to the oncoming and subsequent traffic, as you could leave your lane when you steer and thereby endanger other road users.
Also make sure that no other vehicle wants to leave its parking space to avoid accidents.

question_text: Before which sign must you maintain a distance of at least 10 m, if it would otherwise be concealed by your vehicle?

options.text: Diagonal cross
Stop. Give way.
No stopping

comment: In front of signs such as the diagonal crosses, light signals or the sign "Stop! Yield to cross traffic", you at least have to keep a distance of 10 meters. This is especially necessary if they are going to be covered by your vehicle. For example, you are allowed to come to a stop in front of a stop sign. Behind it, however, stopping is prohibited.

question_text: You want to park on the right-hand side edge of the carriageway. How big is the mandatory minimum distance between your vehicle and the solid lane boundary line?
comment: If a minimum distance of 3 meters to the lane boundary line is observed when parking, the parked car will not present an obstacle.
